chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim and al-Ḥalabī both narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Hajj is in well-known months; so whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, then there shall be no obscenity, no sin, and no disputation in the Hajj."

He عليه السلام said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated a condition upon the people and stipulated for them a condition. So whoever fulfills for Him, Allah fulfills for him." They both said to him, "What is that which He stipulated upon them, and what is that which He stipulated for them?" He said, "As for that which He stipulated upon them, it is His saying: 'Hajj is in well-known months; so whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, then there shall be no obscenity, no sin, and no disputation in the Hajj.' And as for what He stipulated for them, it is His saying: 'So whoever hastens in two days, then there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, then there is no sin upon him, for the one who is Godwary.'" He said: "He returns and there is no sin for him."

They both said to him, "What do you say about one who is afflicted with sinfulness—what is upon him?" He عليه السلام said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not assigned for him a fixed penalty; he seeks forgiveness from Allah and recites the talbiyah."

They both said to him, "Then one who is afflicted with disputation—what is upon him?" He عليه السلام said: "If he disputes more than two times, then upon the one who is correct is blood-sacrifice that he pours forth: a sheep; and upon the one who is mistaken is a cow."

key_terms.اتَّقَىٰ: having taqwa; being Godwary in fulfilling the rites
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: the pilgrimage, here referring to the rites whose conduct is being regulated
key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial blood-offering due as expiation
key_terms.رَفَثَ: obscene or sexual speech prohibited during hajj
key_terms.فُسُوقَ: sinful conduct or disobedience during the state of pilgrimage
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُ: he seeks Allah’s forgiveness for the violation
key_terms.يُلَبِّي: he recites the talbiyah during pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on fusuq and jidal during hajj according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains Qur'an 2:197 as containing both obligations upon the pilgrim in ihram and a divine assurance of forgiveness for the Godwary pilgrim. It clarifies that fusuq during hajj requires seeking forgiveness and continuing the talbiyah, while repeated jidal carries sacrificial liability.
